result: CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin have a mean residence time of ~24 days (~3 weeks), are replaced at ~2% per day from precursors, self-renew every 6-7 weeks, and have clonal half-lives of just over a month.
evaluation: Claims C2-C4, C28, C30, C32-C33, and C36 collectively describe the kinetic parameters of skin TRM derived from mathematical modeling of dual fate-mapping data (Figure 2C, Figure 3). The convergence of independent validation using Ki67 expression (C43, C45) and the consistency across multiple analytical approaches strongly support these quantitative estimates.

result: CD69+CD4+ TRM in lamina propria have shorter residence times (~14 days, ~2 weeks), are maintained largely by immigration at 4-6% per day, divide less frequently (every 7-9 weeks), and have shorter clonal half-lives of ~2 weeks.
evaluation: Claims C5-C6, C29, C34-C35, and C37 describe LP TRM kinetics from the same modeling framework applied to skin. The estimates are internally consistent, validated by independent Ki67-based calculations (C44, C45), and show clear tissue-specific differences from skin TRM, supporting the robustness of the findings.

result: CD69+CD4+ TRM in both skin and LP derive from circulating effector-memory T cells, with skin TRM likely developing via a local CD69− intermediate through a division-linked transition.
evaluation: Claims C7, C40-C42, and C59 describe precursor relationships identified through model comparison analysis (Figure 4A). The model weighting approach (LOO-IC) provides quantitative support for these developmental pathways, with lymph node EM strongly favored as precursor to tissue EM, and CD69− cells favored as precursors to CD69+ TRM in skin (66% model support for division-linked transition).

result: CD4+ TRM are not intrinsically long-lived but are sustained by both self-renewal and supplementation from circulating precursors, with distinct contributions of these processes in skin versus LP.
evaluation: Claims C46-C47 and C60 represent the main conclusions synthesizing the quantitative findings. These are well-supported by the comprehensive kinetic data (C2-C6, C28-C37), the model comparison results (C40-C42), and the convergence of multiple analytical approaches (C43-C45). The tissue-specific differences are clearly demonstrated.

result: CD4+ T cell subsets in skin and LP were at homeostatic steady state during the chase period.
evaluation: Claims C23 and C50 describe the steady-state assumption underlying the modeling. This is supported by the lack of significant changes in cell numbers with mouse age (Figure 2A-B, p>0.39) or time since tamoxifen treatment (p>0.24), providing empirical justification for the equilibrium assumption.

result: mTom expression within skin and LP CD4+ T cell subsets declined slowly (7-8 fold over one year), indicating continuous replacement from precursors.
evaluation: Claims C24-C25 describe a key observation from the Cd4-FR experiments (Figure 2C). The slow decline in mTom+ cells directly demonstrates ongoing replacement, as a closed population at steady state would maintain constant label frequencies. This observation is fundamental to the subsequent modeling.

result: Ki67 expression in YFP+ and YFP− TRM populations converged over time, with Ki67 expression duration estimated at ~3 days, consistent with homogeneous rates of division and loss.
evaluation: Claims C26-C27 describe observed Ki67 convergence kinetics (Figure 2C), while C38-C39 interpret these findings. The ~3-day Ki67 duration estimate is consistent with prior literature (C19) and the convergence pattern supports the model assumption of kinetic homogeneity within each tissue subset.

result: Independent validation using Ki67 expression frequencies and replacement rates yielded residence time estimates of 22-28 days for skin and 14-25 days for LP, in good agreement with model fitting results.
evaluation: Claims C43-C45 describe an independent validation approach using a simpler approximation method. The agreement between this method and the full model fitting (C28-C29) provides strong cross-validation of the residence time estimates and increases confidence in the modeling framework.

result: The rate of replacement of skin TRM (~2% per day) is comparable to rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets.
evaluation: Claim C31 compares the estimated skin TRM replacement rate to previously published rates for circulating memory cells (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024). This comparison is appropriate and the similarity suggests common regulatory mechanisms, though the claim relies on the accuracy of both current and cited estimates.

result: The Ki67-DIVN and Cd4-FR reporter systems enable tracking of dividing cells and CD4+ T cells, respectively, with their descendants through heritable fluorescent markers.
evaluation: Claims C62-C65 describe the genetic reporter systems used. These are established tools previously characterized (Bullock et al., 2024; Gossel et al., 2017; Miller et al., 2018) and the descriptions are consistent with known mechanisms of Cre-lox recombination and tamoxifen-inducible systems.

result: Less than 3% of cells recovered from tissue samples were positive for in vivo Thy1.2 labeling, validating the tissue localization approach.
evaluation: Claim C66 provides validation of the tissue localization method. The low frequency of labeled cells in tissues (<3%) compared to high labeling efficiency in circulation (>99%, Anderson et al., 2014) demonstrates effective discrimination between tissue-resident and circulating cells, supporting the validity of the experimental approach.

result: The large antigenic burden within the small intestine may drive higher levels of TRM recruitment and clonal erosion in LP compared to skin.
evaluation: Claim C48 is explicitly speculative ('we speculate') and proposes a mechanistic explanation for observed tissue differences. While the speculation is reasonable given the known antigenic environment of the gut, no direct evidence is provided to test this hypothesis. The claim appropriately acknowledges uncertainty ('The basis of this difference is unclear').

result: The mathematical model explains stable TRM maintenance without invoking homeostatic niches, predicting that changes in influx rates lead to new equilibria at different cell densities.
evaluation: Claims C51, C54-C55 describe properties and predictions of the mathematical model. C51 is a logical consequence of steady-state dynamics. C54-C55 represent model-based inferences that are mathematically sound given the model structure, though experimental validation of these predictions (e.g., through perturbation experiments) would strengthen support.

result: Tissue-specific influx may contribute to differential longevity of immunity at different barrier sites, particularly if there are competitive limits to TRM occupancy.
evaluation: Claim C61 is speculative ('may contribute') and conditional ('particularly if'). While the observed tissue-specific differences in influx rates (C30, C35) and clonal half-lives (C36-C37) provide a basis for this hypothesis, no direct evidence is presented linking these kinetic differences to immunity duration or demonstrating competitive limits to TRM occupancy.

result: Background context on TRM biology, prior studies of TRM dynamics, and methodological approaches for studying cell kinetics.
evaluation: Claims C1, C9-C19, C67-C72 provide literature context and are supported by appropriate citations. These establish the knowledge gaps (C67-C68), methodological challenges (C69), and prior findings that motivate the current study. The citations appear appropriate for the claims made.

result: Discussion of potential confounding factors, alternative contexts, and limitations of the findings.
evaluation: Claims C49, C52-C53, C56-C58 acknowledge limitations and discuss alternative scenarios. C49 and C52 make reasonable inferences about the experimental system. C53 appropriately notes that findings may differ in other contexts (acute infections). C56-C57 cite relevant prior work on CD8+ TRM, while C58 acknowledges gaps in knowledge about CD4+ TRM. These represent appropriate scientific caution.
